# vite-plugin-tsl-precompile

> Capture TSL from real three.js WebGPU renders, validate the artifacts at
> build time, and optionally replay verified WGSL without NodeBuilder.

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/Makio64/vite-plugin-tsl-precompile
Agent skill: https://makio64.github.io/vite-plugin-tsl-precompile/agent/integrate-tsl-precompile/SKILL.md
Generated evidence: https://makio64.github.io/vite-plugin-tsl-precompile/examples.html

## Fit

- Requires Node >=24.0.0, Vite >=6.4.3 <9, `WebGPURenderer`, TSL NodeMaterials, and
  exactly `three@0.185.1` for the current alpha.
- The plugin and runtime must use matching releases.
- Do not silently migrate a WebGL-only, non-Vite, or non-TSL app.

## Working style

- Delegated: run the full execution contract end to end and return the evidence.
- Review-first: before application edits, report the fit decision, doctor
  findings, proposed files, and route/state/render-topology capture matrix.
  Preserve compatibility mode and present slim mode as a separate later change.

In either style, do not stop at dependency installation or a successful build.
Generated artifacts and a real WebGPU production preview are part of done.

## Install

Before mutation, inspect the lockfile, Vite config, renderer, TSL materials, and
current `three`/`@types/three`. Stop without installing when the app is not a fit
or the exact Three pin would be an unapproved migration.

The first alpha packages are not published to npm yet. If the registry returns
404, stop and say so; never substitute a similarly named package. Once published,
use the project's package manager. pnpm:

    pnpm add -D vite-plugin-tsl-precompile@alpha
    pnpm add @tsl-precompile/runtime@alpha three@0.185.1 --save-exact
    pnpm add -D @types/three@0.185.1 --save-exact  # TypeScript only
    pnpm exec tsl-precompile-install-skill --json
    pnpm exec tsl-precompile-doctor --json --source src

Replace or repeat `--source` for the JavaScript/TypeScript roots found during
the audit; `src` is an example, not a required layout.

Doctor readiness covers version, setup, source, and artifact checks only; it
does not prove route/state/render-topology coverage, a passing production build
or WebGPU preview, or that slim mode is safe.

Then ask:

    Use $integrate-tsl-precompile end to end. Start in compatibility mode with
    the default automatic NodeMaterial detection. Add explicit markers only for
    stable semantic names or constructors that cannot be detected. Capture every
    real render path. Verify and commit a non-zero artifacts/ set. Build and
    smoke-test production. Do not enable slim until every compatibility gate
    passes.

The installer defaults to `.agents/skills/integrate-tsl-precompile`. It also
accepts `--target codex`, `--target claude`, or a project-relative skill root.

## Execution contract

1. Audit config, renderer bootstrap, NodeMaterials, routes, and render
   topologies before editing.
2. Start with `tslPrecompile()` compatibility mode.
3. Register the live renderer once with `setupPrecompile({ renderer })`; await
   `renderer.init()` and `setup.ready`.
4. Keep the default automatic detection for direct `new *NodeMaterial(...)`
   constructors. Add stable `material.precompile('project-global-name')`
   overrides only where semantic names help or detection cannot see a
   constructor.
5. Run dev and exercise every real route and materially different state.
6. Never fabricate or hand-edit generated artifacts. Commit them.
7. Require both gates:

       pnpm exec tsl-precompile-verify --source src --source-root . artifacts
       pnpm build

8. In browser automation, use `setup.captureStatus()` plus
   `setup.waitForCaptureSettled({ since: status })` instead of a fixed sleep.
9. Smoke-test production in a WebGPU browser. Only then consider
   `tslPrecompile({ slim: 'source' })` and repeat capture, build, and preview.

## Done means

- Matching plugin/runtime versions and exact supported three.js.
- Every intended material is covered by an automatic or explicit marker.
- Every reachable route and material, background, environment, shadow,
  post-processing, MRT, renderer-output, and compute topology was rendered.
- Verification reports a non-zero artifact family.
- Production build and representative WebGPU preview pass.
- The handoff states compatibility or separately proven slim mode.
